request.prompt:
You are an independent evaluation judge. Grade the proposed remedy, not the
writing style of this prompt. A good remedy changes a concrete future behavior,
is broad enough to cover the failure mode without becoming a platitude, uses a
real `Use when ...` trigger when it is a skill, leaks no evidence-specific
project nouns into the remedy text, and uses the cheapest adequate remedy type.

Score every dimension from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Give exactly one concise
sentence of justification for each score. Do not infer facts that are absent.

PROPOSAL:
{
  "failure_statement": "Explicit task constraints were lost during implementation.",
  "remedy_content": {
    "target": "global",
    "text": "Before making changes, restate and preserve every explicit scope, file, and tool constraint from the request."
  },
  "remedy_type": "claude-md",
  "routing_rationale": "A standing one-line instruction is cheaper than a procedural skill."
}

response.result: {"actionability":{"score":2,"justification":"\"Restate and preserve\" gives no concrete mechanism (e.g., a checklist to output, a point to verify against) so compliance can't be checked and behavior change is unclear."},"generality_without_vagueness":{"score":2,"justification":"Covers the broad failure class but is phrased as a generic maxim (\"every explicit scope, file, and tool constraint\") with no concrete criteria, tipping into platitude territory."},"trigger_quality":{"score":2,"justification":"As a global always-on claude-md line it has no scoping trigger (e.g., long/multi-step tasks, delegation, late-context edits) to target when constraint-loss actually occurs, risking dilution among other standing instructions."},"leakage":{"score":5,"justification":"Text is fully generic with no project-specific nouns, file names, or tool names leaked from the evidence."},"routing_fitness":{"score":3,"justification":"claude-md is the cheapest plausible vehicle for a standing reminder, but the vague failure_statement gives little basis to confirm this generic instruction actually addresses the real root cause rather than just restating the symptom."}}

actionability.justification: "Restate and preserve" gives no concrete mechanism (e.g., a checklist to output, a point to verify against) so compliance can't be checked and behavior change is unclear.

generality_without_vagueness.justification: Covers the broad failure class but is phrased as a generic maxim ("every explicit scope, file, and tool constraint") with no concrete criteria, tipping into platitude territory.

leakage.justification: Text is fully generic with no project-specific nouns, file names, or tool names leaked from the evidence.

routing_fitness.justification: claude-md is the cheapest plausible vehicle for a standing reminder, but the vague failure_statement gives little basis to confirm this generic instruction actually addresses the real root cause rather than just restating the symptom.

trigger_quality.justification: As a global always-on claude-md line it has no scoping trigger (e.g., long/multi-step tasks, delegation, late-context edits) to target when constraint-loss actually occurs, risking dilution among other standing instructions.
